4. Mti Principles

   As a normal search radar system, the
AN/TPS-1D is similar in theory of operation
to typical pulsed search type radar equipments.
A serious limitation of the normal search type
radar is that the returns from large stationary
targets make it difficult or impossible to detect
airborne targets flying over stationary targets
when the returns appear in the same positions
on the indicators. The inclusion of mti circuits

                                                CHAPTER 12

               TRANSMITTING SYSTEM TROUBLESHOOTING AND REPAIR

       Warning: Extremely dangerous voltages exist in Radar Modulator MD-144/TPS-1D and
Radar Receiver-Transmitter RT-212/TPS-1D.

       1. Defeat interlocks only for the purpose of making observations within a unit.
       2. Do not make voltage measurements in the modulator or receiver-transmitter high-voltage
circuits.
      3. Do not make waveform checks in the modulator or receiver-transmitter high-voltage circuits
except at the jacks or test points provided.
      4. Before making resistance measurements or coming in contact with any high-voltage
components in the receiver-transmitter, turn the equipment off and disconnect cable from PULSE
INPUT jack J505.
       5. Before making resistance measurements or coming in contact with any high-voltage
components in the modulator, turn the equipment off and ground L152 and the junction of the
leads to the plate caps of V153 and V154 with a shorting bar.
       Caution: If the transmitter will not operate because of the operation of protective relay K151,
do not readjust balance adjustment R168 to correct the situation; damage to the equipment may
result. Refer to paragraph 229 for adjustment procedure for R168.

making resistance measurements in the high-voltage power supply chassis.

given in Section II of the glossaries of TM            targets. A quantitative measurement in
